attempted_claim: Let Gamma satisfy the Standing Assumptions of Nguyen–Tran: Gamma is connected, triangle-free, planar, has at least 5 vertices, and has no separating vertex or edge. Assume Gamma is non-CFS. Then G_Gamma is hyperbolic relative to CFS right-angled Coxeter subgroups and its (global) divergence satisfies Div(G_Gamma) asymptotic exp. Let Spec(G_Gamma) denote the divergence spectrum in the sense of Tran: the set of asymptotic-classes of lower divergences ldiv_alpha as alpha ranges over Morse bi-infinite geodesics in the Davis complex / Cayley graph. Is Spec(G_Gamma) = {[r^2], [exp]}, with [r^2] realized by Morse geodesics in CFS peripheral subgroups and [exp] realized by a non-peripheral (e.g. periodic) Morse geodesic? In particular, if Gamma,Gamma' are two such non-CFS planar graphs whose collections of maximal CFS peripheral subgroups have non-bisimilar visual decomposition trees, do G_Gamma and G_Gamma' have the same spectrum, so that the divergence spectrum is blind inside the planar exponential regime, or does it refine the peripheral tree structure and hence distinguish quasi-isometry classes with the same global exponential divergence?
decisive_failure: originality: Headline Spec(G_C5)={[exp]} is mechanically implied by prior stronger facts: Moussong hyperbolicity for square-free C5 plus Tran Example 4.7 that a one-ended hyperbolic group has exp-only spectrum. Tran's general theorem substantively implies the C5 instance without stating C5 verbatim, so under the substantive-implication rule originality FAILS. The C5 non-CFS/hyperbolic facts are standard criteria applications, not new boundaries. value: ADMISSION_DEFECT: the admitted universal two-point wording presupposed non-empty CFS peripherals realizing [r^2], but the Standing-Assumptions class contains hyperbolic empty-peripheral members with C5 the smallest (n=5) case. Refuting the universal by C5's vacuous peripheral clause is vacuity/cheap small-instance mismatch, not a substantive spectral advance. The singleton itself is a direct corollary of Tran's hyperbolic principle and the coarse non-blindness was already shown by Tran's infinite exp-divergence family with distinct spectra.
